🇲🇽🎒 <u>2,500-PESO SCHOOL SUPPLY SUPPORT STARTS LANDING FOR MILLIONS OF STUDENTS</u>

Deposits of the annual 2,500-peso support for school supplies and uniforms began Monday for public primary school students, staggered by last name through August 14, Becas Benito Juárez coordinator Julio León Trujillo announced.

The support is universal: every child in a public primary school gets it, straight to the family.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>1.5 MILLION LITERS OF STOLEN FUEL SEIZED IN VERACRUZ AS SECURITY CABINET SWEEPS 10 STATES</u>

From July 31 to August 2, Mexico's security cabinet hit 10 states. In Tuzamapan, Veracruz, the National Guard, Army, FGR and Pemex's own security seized 1.5 million liters of fuel, 49 containers, trucks and an entire property used for huachicol.

The fuel-theft crackdown the old regime calls "persecution" keeps delivering.

🇲🇽🥇 <u>MEXICAN STUDENT WINS GOLD AT THE WORLD'S TOP UNIVERSITY MATH COMPETITION</u>

Emiliano Fernández Almazán, a Universidad Veracruzana student from Xalapa, just took gold at the 33rd International Mathematics Competition for University Students in Bulgaria — 80 points and a top-nine finish against the best university mathematicians on the planet.

A product of Mexico's free public universities.
banner: MEXICAN STUDENT WINS WORLD MATH GOLD

🇲🇽📈 <u>BANXICO SURVEY: GROWTH FORECAST UP, INFLATION FORECAST DOWN</u>

Private analysts consulted by Banco de México raised their 2026 growth forecast from 1.10% to 1.20% and cut their inflation forecast from 4.20% to 4.00%, El Economista reports. They also see the peso closing the year at 17.88 per dollar and 305,000 new formal jobs. After a 2.1% second quarter that beat every forecast, the "experts" keep quietly revising upward.
banner: BANXICO SURVEY: GDP UP, INFLATION DOWN

text:
🇲🇽🌽 <u>FREE FERTILIZER PROGRAM HITS 95.9% OF ITS NATIONAL TARGET</u>

Mexico's Fertilizantes para el Bienestar has reached 2,037,000 small producers — 95.9% of the goal — with 970,700 tons delivered across 3.5 million hectares, three-quarters of it maize. And 354,518 beneficiaries are indigenous women, 43.5% of all women supported. Food sovereignty isn't a slogan; it's logistics.

🇲🇽📺 <u>CANAL ONCE RECOVERED; 70 YEARS OF PUBLIC TV ARCHIVE UNDER REVIEW</u>

Canal Once — Mexico's public broadcaster, held by a student sit-in since May 20 — was peacefully retaken by its own workers. Education Secretary Mario Delgado confirmed possible damage to the channel's historic archive: "It is not possible for a channel that belongs to the people of Mexico to remain seized by a group of youths." Dialogue tables continue; the occupation doesn't.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>6.7 MILLION STUDENTS GET 2,500 PESOS FOR SCHOOL SUPPLIES</u>

Mexico's back-to-school support started hitting accounts Monday: 2,500 pesos for supplies and uniforms for 6,694,988 public primary students — a 16.7-billion-peso investment. The broader scholarship system now covers 19.6 million students with 93.7 billion pesos, and the Rita Cetina primary scholarship has already delivered 95.1% of its 5 million cards.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>"VOICES THAT PREDICT OUR FAILURE": MEXICO'S NEW SUPREME COURT ANSWERS WITH RESULTS</u>

One year into the elected judiciary, Chief Justice Hugo Aguilar called out those who "augur the failure" of the new Court: 2,243 cases resolved in public session, just 56 left of the 1,471 inherited from the old court. Minister Lenia Batres landed the number: 100% of cases are now resolved in public — before the reform, it was 5%.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO AND JAPAN MOVE TO DEEPEN TRADE TIES</u>

While Washington waves tariffs, Mexico keeps diversifying. Mexico and Japan agreed to strengthen commercial ties — 1,600 Japanese companies already operate in Mexico, generating close to 350,000 jobs. The world's fourth-largest economy isn't waiting for permission to bet on Mexico.
